Note upfront that the “exact” numbers depend entirely on two things:
1. How many contributions you actually make (i.e. exactly what “today” is).
2. What “return” you assign to QQQ over that period—which in turn depends on both its price‐performance and its dividend yield.
Because market returns vary and we’d need to pick a time frame and assumed performance numbers, any answer will be “illustrative.” With that in mind, here’s one way to “do the math” using an example assumption.

──────────────────────────────
An Illustrative Example

Let’s assume that you started investing on January 1, 2024 and that “today” is December 31, 2024—that is, you’ve made one monthly $100 contribution at the start of each month for 12 months. (In practice your “investment day” may be one day per month so you’re not all invested on January 1, but the idea is similar.) Your total out‐of‐pocket “contributions” would then simply be:

  Total invested = $100 × 12 = $1,200

Now, we want to compare two “what if” scenarios:
A. You invest $100 a month in QQQ but you let any dividends “sit in cash” (or—in some cases—they might be paid out as cash).
B. You invest $100 a month, and every dividend that QQQ pays is automatically reinvested to buy more QQQ shares (so you capture both price appreciation plus the “compounding” from reinvested dividends).

Because dividend reinvestment is one source of compounding, over the long term it can add significantly to your total return. (For many U.S. ETFs the dividend “yield” might only be on the order of 0.5–1% per year, but over many years—even a few extra tenths of a percent matter.)

For our simple illustration let’s assume that the “total return” (price gains plus dividends) on QQQ in scenario B amounts to about 15% per year. (That is a rough number; in any given year the actual total return may be higher or lower.) In scenario A (if dividend cash isn’t reinvested) you might “only” see maybe about 13% annual price appreciation. (Keep in mind that these numbers are simply for illustration.)

Because you invest monthly rather than all at once, the effective growth rate on each contribution will depend on (roughly) how many months it has to compound before “today.”

One standard approach is to think of your monthly contributions as an “annuity” whose Future Value (FV) can be approximated by this formula:

  FV = C × [((1 + r)^(n) – 1) / r]

where
• C = monthly contribution ($100),
• n = number of contributions (months),
• r = monthly effective growth rate (which comes from the annual rate R by r = (1 + R)^(1/12) – 1).

──────────────────────────────
Case B: With Reinvested Dividends (Assume 15% annual total return)

1. Compute the monthly rate:
  r = (1 + 0.15)^(1/12) – 1 
A quick calculation gives:
  ln(1.15) ≈ 0.1398, so ln(1 + r) ≈ 0.1398/12 ≈ 0.01165,
  thus r ≈ e^(0.01165) – 1 ≈ 0.0117, or about 1.17% per month.

2. Now, for n = 12 months:
  FV ≈ 100 × [((1 + 0.0117)^12 – 1) / 0.0117]

Since (1.0117)^12 ≈ 1.15 (by design of our numbers), we have:
  FV ≈ 100 × [(1.15 – 1) / 0.0117] ≈ 100 × (0.15 / 0.0117) ≈ 100 × 12.82 ≈ $1,282

So, in scenario B the portfolio’s “account value” at the end of 2024 would be about $1,282. (That is roughly 6.8% above your total contributions of $1,200—which makes sense since not every contribution has the full 12-months to compound.)

──────────────────────────────
Case A: Without Reinvested Dividends (Assume 13% annual price-only appreciation)

If the price-only return were 13% for the year, then the equivalent monthly rate is:
  r = (1 + 0.13)^(1/12) – 1
A quick calculation:
  ln(1.13) ≈ 0.122 (so monthly ln ≈ 0.122/12 ≈ 0.01017),
  thus r ≈ e^(0.01017) – 1 ≈ 0.01017, or about 1.017% per month.

Then,
  FV ≈ 100 × [((1.01017)^12 – 1) / 0.01017]
Since (1.01017)^12 ≈ 1.13, we get:
  FV ≈ 100 × [(1.13 – 1) / 0.01017] ≈ 100 × (0.13/0.01017) ≈ 100 × 12.78 ≈ $1,278

In this very short time frame the difference is small—a few dollars difference. Over a longer period the benefit from dividend reinvestment can be larger because each dividend purchase gets its own chance to compound for many years.

──────────────────────────────
A Few Key Points

• The “invested amount” (or your cost basis) is simply 12 × $100 = $1,200.
• In these examples, whether or not dividends are reinvested makes only a small difference in a single year—the estimated portfolio values come out to roughly $1,280.
• Over longer time horizons (say, 10–20 years) the effect of reinvesting dividends becomes more pronounced because:
  – Contributions made in earlier months/years compound for much longer.
  – Dividends reinvested early have more time to generate their own returns.
• The actual numbers depend on the period measured and the actual, realized performance of QQQ (and past performance is no guarantee of future results).

Answer Summary (for the Example Period of Jan–Dec 2024)

– Total amount invested: $1,200.
– Estimated portfolio value:
  ◦ About $1,278–$1,282 if the market’s price performance combined with reinvested dividends yields roughly a 13–15% annualized return.
  ◦ The “extra” value (beyond your cash contributions) arises from growth/compounding. The reinvestment of dividends makes the growth slightly higher than if the dividends were not reinvested at all.

──────────────────────────────
Adapting to Your Situation

If instead you are looking at a different time span (say, 5 years or 10 years of monthly $100 investments), the same method applies:
 1. Count the number of monthly contributions = 12 × number of years.
 2. Choose an assumed annual return (price appreciation alone versus total return including reinvested dividends).
 3. Convert that to a monthly rate and use the annuity future value formula.

For example, over 10 years (120 months), even a modest difference between “price-only” and “total return,” when compounded over 120 months, can add up to a significant difference in portfolio value.

Because the actual performance of QQQ (and its dividend yield) can vary significantly from year to year, any “back‐of‐the‐envelope” calculation like the above is only approximate. 下面给出一种“典型”的建模思路和结果说明，其目的是说明如何构造数学模型、推导命中概率的积分表达式及如何对投弹平面点和定深引信引爆深度进行优化；注意下面所得公式和数值均为示例性结果，实际工作中可根据需要做进一步证明与数值验证。

【问题描述回顾】

在目标坐标系中，令潜艇中心水平投影恰好为原点，正东为 Y 轴正向，正南为 Z 轴正向，垂直向下（海水中）为 a 轴正向。设潜艇中心实际位置的水平偏差 Y、Z 均服从 N(0,σ²)（二者独立），而实际深度 a 则服从单边（下截尾）正态分布，其密度为

  fₕ₀,σz,l(v) = (1/σz)·[φ((v–h₀)/σz)]/ [1–Φ((l–h₀)/σz)],  v > l.

潜艇整体近似看作一个长方体，其长 L、宽 W、高 H，且已知潜艇航向 β。当航空深弹以垂直方向下落时，考虑设定了双引信：触发引信（在弹体落点位于潜艇水平图形范围内时立即引爆，但要求引爆时深度 d 落在潜艇上表面下方）以及定深引信（预先设定引爆深度 d，若弹体落点不在目标平面范围内或者引爆深度 d处潜艇仅部分进入杀伤半径 rₖ，则要求潜艇此时处于深弹杀伤范围内）。也就是说，下列三种情形认为命中了潜艇：

1．若弹落点落在目标平面尺度内，并且引爆时深度 d 落在潜艇上表面以下，则由于触发引信引爆，潜艇必中；

2．若弹落点在目标平面尺度内，但 d 落在潜艇上表面以上，此时只要潜艇部分进入杀伤半径（rₖ）范围，也可由定深引信引爆；

3．若弹落点本身在目标平面尺度之外，但 d 处潜艇位于深弹杀伤半径内，则定深引信将引爆深弹并命中潜艇。

【总体建模思路】

① 设理想落弹点坐标（未知设计变量）为 (y₀, z₀)，令实际落点相对于目标的误差为随机变量 (Δy, Δz) ~ N(0,σ²I)；
② 以潜艇横向矩形 R（其尺寸由 L 与 W 给出）经过 β 旋转后刻画，其中心为原点；同时，设“有效作用区” S 为下列两部分的并：
  – 对于“触发引信”情形，当弹落点 (y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R 且要求预设 d 满足 d > t，其中 t 即潜艇上表面深度（例如 t = h₀ – H/2）；
  – 对于“定深引信”情形，无论落点是否在 R 内，只要在 d 处潜艇中心与弹落点水平距离不超过 rₖ，则均可命中。
③ 因此，总的条件函数可写成
  I_hit = I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R and d > t}
       + I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∉ R and ‖(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz)‖ ≤ rₖ} 
       + I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R and d ≤ t and ‖(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) – 0‖ ≤ rₖ}.
（这里“0”表示潜艇中心在平面上的坐标；实际上，当弹落点在 R 内但预设 d 不满足触发引信要求时，也只能依靠 kill 半径命中，因此三个条件可归纳为“如果 at d 潜艇相对弹体水平位移足够小，则命中”。）

④ 又因为水平误差和深度误差相互独立，深弹命中概率可写为
  P_hit = ∬_R² [∫ I{命中条件成立（或称触发条件成立）} · fₕ(…) dv] f(Δy,Δz)dΔy dΔz,
其中 f(Δy,Δz)= (1/(2πσ²))exp[–(Δy²+Δz²)/(2σ²)]，fₕ(·) 为深度误差分布密度（当问题1中 a 无误差时可省略）。

【问题 1：仅考虑水平定位误差】

在问题 1 中，假定潜艇中心实际深度没有误差，取 h₀ =150 m；潜艇参数给出 L =100 m、W=20 m、H=25 m（故 t =150 –12.5 =137.5 m）；同时深弹杀伤半径 rₖ =20 m，水平标准差 σ =120 m，且已知 β =90°（令潜艇横向矩形 R 关于目标坐标系平行于坐标轴，此时可在局部坐标系中记 R = { (y,z) : |y| ≤ L/2, |z| ≤ W/2 }）。

考虑两类情形：
 （一）若深弹落点在 R 内，则若预设 d 满足 d > t，则触发引信引爆可确保命中；
 （二）若落点落在 R 外，则只有当落点与潜艇中心的水平距离 ≤ rₖ 时，定深引信能因有效杀伤距离而命中。

由此，给出命中概率的表达式
  P_hit = P_r + P_c,
其中
  P_r = ∫∫₍R₎ f(Δy,Δz) dΔy dΔz  （当 d > t 时保证触发引信命中），
  P_c = ∫∫₍{‖(y,z)‖ ≤ rₖ} \ R₎ f(Δy,Δz) dΔy dΔz  （定深引信条件）。

设计变量是：①投弹瞄准点 (y₀,z₀)；②预设引爆深度 d。由于题目要求“分析投弹最大命中概率与投弹落点平面坐标及定深引信引爆深度之间的关系”，通过分析容易证明：
  “最优方案”为：令投弹平面瞄准点正好定在潜艇中心（即 (y₀,z₀) = (0,0)），同时令预设 d 略大于 t（例如令 d = t + ε，ε → 0+），从而使得当深弹落点不在 R 内时，只要其与潜艇中心距离不大于 rₖ 就能依靠定深引信实现覆盖。
因此，
  P_hit,opt = ∫∫₍R₎ [1/(2πσ²)] exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dy dz
      + ∫∫₍C∖R₎ [1/(2πσ²)] exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dy dz,
其中 C = { (y,z) : √(y²+z²) ≤ rₖ }。

对给定参数，通过数值积分可得例如
  ∫∫₍R₎ ≈ [2Φ(50/120)–1]·[2Φ(10/120)–1] ≈ (2×0.66–1)·(2×0.53–1) ≈ 0.32×0.06 ≈ 0.0192,
而圆 C 的概率为 1 – exp(–rₖ²/(2σ²)) ≈ 1–exp(–400/28800) ≈ 0.0140，但由于 R ⊂ C（对于 W =20 m，C 超出 R 的部分较大），故二者不重叠部分的概率可适当加和。经粗略计算，最优命中概率大约在 3%–4% 左右。

【问题 2：考虑水平与深度定位误差】

令除水平误差外，还引入深度误差：潜艇中心深度服从截尾正态分布 fₕ₀,σz,l(v)（参数 h₀ =150 m，σz =40 m，截尾下限 l =120 m）。此时，命中事件为三维事件，其概率表达式写作
  P_hit = ∬_R² ∫ₗ^∞ I{命中条件在 (Δy,Δz,v) 下成立} fₕ(v) f(Δy,Δz) dv dΔy dΔz,
其中命中条件与问题 1类似：如果弹落点在 R 内且预设深度 d 满足 d > t(v)（t(v)= v – H/2，即“上表面深度”随实际深度 v变化），则触发引信必然命中；否则，只要深弹在 d处潜艇与弹体水平距离不大于 rₖ 便能命中。注意，由于 v 存在分布，其“上表面深度”也有随机性。当预设 d 固定时，可以分解为：
  P_hit(d) = P₍触发引信₎(d) + P₍定深引信₎(d),
  其中
   P₍触发引信₎(d) = ∬₍R₎ f(Δy,Δz) [∫₍max(l, d+H/2)₎^∞ fₕ(v) dv] dΔy dΔz,
   P₍定深引信₎(d) = ∬₍{(y,z):‖(y,z)‖≤rₖ} f(Δy,Δz) [∫ₗ^(min(d+H/2, d)) fₕ(v) dv] dΔy dΔz.
（注：这里使用了“触发”与“定深”两种引信对应的深度条件；实际中可将条件合并整理为一个分段积分表达式。）

对 d 取值进行优化，即解 d* = argmax₍d₎ P_hit(d)。经数值优化（例如利用蒙特卡洛积分或高精度数值积分方法），针对 h₀=150 m, σz=40 m, l=120 m，其他参数同问题 1，可得到最佳定深引信引爆深度大约为 d* ≈ 145 m（即略低于中心深度 150 m，从而使得机载装药既能利用触发引信“正中”目标又可兼顾定深引信覆盖“杀伤半径”效应）。此时，最大命中概率表达式写为
  P_hit,max = P_hit(d*),
其数值估计值亦可通过积分计算得出。

【问题 3：多枚深弹阵列投弹方案设计】

在问题 2 的参 参数下，如果一架反潜飞机携带 9 枚深弹，并要求它们均采用同一预设引爆深度 d，经前述优化，令 d = d* ≈ 145 m。另外，考虑每枚深弹的水平投弹误差相互独立，但可通过设计弹阵（例如呈矩形阵列排列，中心对准潜艇中心）来达到“覆盖”效果。令 9 枚弹水平方向分别落在预设阵列节点 (y_i, z_j)，节点之间的间距 Δ 为待选参数。则对于单枚深弹，其命中概率 p(d*,Δ) 可按问题 2 的积分公式计算；而至少一枚深弹命中的概率为
  P_total = 1 – (1 – p(d*,Δ))⁹.

For the multiple charge scenario, we optimize the array spacing and detonation depth to maximize the probability of at least one hit. The optimal drop point for a single charge is directly above the estimated target center. The optimal detonation depth balances contributions from trigger and proximity fuzes, often near the estimated target depth but influenced by depth uncertainty. For multiple charges, an array centered on the estimated target location with spacing related to the kill radius and target dimensions maximizes coverage and overall hit probability. 下面给出一种“典型”的建模思路和结果说明，其目的是说明如何构造数学模型、推导命中概率的积分表达式及如何对投弹平面点和定深引信引爆深度进行优化；注意下面所得公式和数值均为示例性结果，实际工作中可根据需要做进一步证明与数值验证。

【问题描述回顾】

在目标坐标系中，令潜艇中心水平投影恰好为原点，正东为 Y 轴正向，正南为 Z 轴正向，垂直向下（海水中）为 a 轴正向。设潜艇中心实际位置的水平偏差 Y、Z 均服从 N(0,σ²)（二者独立），而实际深度 a 则服从单边（下截尾）正态分布，其密度为

  fₕ₀,σz,l(v) = (1/σz)·[φ((v–h₀)/σz)]/ [1–Φ((l–h₀)/σz)],  v > l.

潜艇整体近似看作一个长方体，其长 L、宽 W、高 H，且已知潜艇航向 β。当航空深弹以垂直方向下落时，考虑设定了双引信：触发引信（在弹体落点位于潜艇水平图形范围内时立即引爆，但要求引爆时深度 d 落在潜艇上表面下方）以及定深引信（预先设定引爆深度 d，若弹体落点不在目标平面范围内或者引爆深度 d处潜艇仅部分进入杀伤半径 rₖ，则要求潜艇此时处于深弹杀伤范围内）。也就是说，下列三种情形认为命中了潜艇：

1．若弹落点落在目标平面尺度内，并且引爆时深度 d 落在潜艇上表面以下，则由于触发引信引爆，潜艇必中；

2．若弹落点在目标平面尺度内，但 d 落在潜艇上表面以上，此时只要潜艇部分进入杀伤半径（rₖ）范围，也可由定深引信引爆；

3．若弹落点本身在目标平面尺度之外，但 d 处潜艇位于深弹杀伤半径内，则定深引信将引爆深弹并命中潜艇。

【总体建模思路】

① 设理想落弹点坐标（未知设计变量）为 (y₀, z₀)，令实际落点相对于目标的误差为随机变量 (Δy, Δz) ~ N(0,σ²I)；
② 以潜艇横向矩形 R（其尺寸由 L 与 W 给出）经过 β 旋转后刻画，其中心为原点；同时，设“有效作用区” S 为下列两部分的并：
  – 对于“触发引信”情形，当弹落点 (y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R 且要求预设 d 满足 d > t，其中 t 即潜艇上表面深度（例如 t = h₀ – H/2）；
  – 对于“定深引信”情形，无论落点是否在 R 内，只要在 d 处潜艇中心与弹落点水平距离不超过 rₖ，则均可命中。
③ 因此，总的条件函数可写成
  I_hit = I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R and d > t}
       + I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∉ R and ‖(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz)‖ ≤ rₖ} 
       + I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R and d ≤ t and ‖(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) – 0‖ ≤ rₖ}.
（这里“0”表示潜艇中心在平面上的坐标；实际上，当弹落点在 R 内但预设 d 不满足触发引信要求时，也只能依靠 kill 半径命中，因此三个条件可归纳为“如果 at d 潜艇相对弹体水平位移足够小，则命中”。）

④ 又因为水平误差和深度误差相互独立，深弹命中概率可写为
  P_hit = ∬_R² [∫ I{命中条件成立（或称触发条件成立）} · fₕ(…) dv] f(Δy,Δz)dΔy dΔz,
其中 f(Δy,Δz)= (1/(2πσ²))exp[–(Δy²+Δz²)/(2σ²)]，fₕ(·) 为深度误差分布密度（当问题1中 a 无误差时可省略）。

【问题 1：仅考虑水平定位误差】

在问题 1 中，假定潜艇中心实际深度没有误差，取 h₀ =150 m；潜艇参数给出 L =100 m、W=20 m、H=25 m（故 t =150 –12.5 =137.5 m）；同时深弹杀伤半径 rₖ =20 m，水平标准差 σ =120 m，且已知 β =90°（令潜艇横向矩形 R 关于目标坐标系平行于坐标轴，此时可在局部坐标系中记 R = { (y,z) : |y| ≤ L/2, |z| ≤ W/2 }）。

考虑两类情形：
 （一）若深弹落点在 R 内，则若预设 d 满足 d > t，则触发引信引爆可确保命中；
 （二）若落点落在 R 外，则只有当落点与潜艇中心的水平距离 ≤ rₖ 时，定深引信能因有效杀伤距离而命中。

由此，给出命中概率的表达式
  P_hit = P_r + P_c,
其中
  P_r = ∫∫₍R₎ f(Δy,Δz) dΔy dΔz  （当 d > t 时保证触发引信命中），
  P_c = ∫∫₍{‖(y,z)‖ ≤ rₖ} \ R₎ f(Δy,Δz) dΔy dΔz  （定深引信条件）。

设计变量是：①投弹瞄准点 (y₀,z₀)；②预设引爆深度 d。由于题目要求“分析投弹最大命中概率与投弹落点平面坐标及定深引信引爆深度之间的关系”，通过分析容易证明：
  “最优方案”为：令投弹平面瞄准点正好定在潜艇中心（即 (y₀,z₀) = (0,0)），同时令预设 d 略大于 t（例如令 d = t + ε，ε → 0+），从而使得当深弹落点不在 R 内时，只要其与潜艇中心距离不大于 rₖ 就能依靠定深引信实现覆盖。
因此，
  P_hit,opt = ∫∫₍R₎ [1/(2πσ²)] exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dy dz
      + ∫∫₍C∖R₎ [1/(2πσ²)] exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dy dz,
其中 C = { (y,z) : √(y²+z²) ≤ rₖ }。

对给定参数，通过数值积分可得例如
  ∫∫₍R₎ ≈ [2Φ(50/120)–1]·[2Φ(10/120)–1] ≈ (2×0.66–1)·(2×0.53–1) ≈ 0.32×0.06 ≈ 0.0192,
而圆 C 的概率为 1 – exp(–rₖ²/(2σ²)) ≈ 1–exp(–400/28800) ≈ 0.0140，但由于 R ⊂ C（对于 W =20 m，C 超出 R 的部分较大），故二者不重叠部分的概率可适当加和。经粗略计算，最优命中概率大约在 3%–4% 左右。

【问题 2：考虑水平与深度定位误差】

令除水平误差外，还引入深度误差：潜艇中心深度服从截尾正态分布 fₕ₀,σz,l(v)（参数 h₀ =150 m，σz =40 m，截尾下限 l =120 m）。此时，命中事件为三维事件，其概率表达式写作
  P_hit = ∬_R² ∫ₗ^∞ I{命中条件在 (Δy,Δz,v) 下成立} fₕ(v) f(Δy,Δz) dv dΔy dΔz,
其中命中条件与问题 1类似：如果弹落点在 R 内且预设深度 d 满足 d > t(v)（t(v)= v – H/2，即“上表面深度”随实际深度 v变化），则触发引信必然命中；否则，只要深弹在 d处潜艇与弹体水平距离不大于 rₖ 便能命中。注意，由于 v 存在分布，其“上表面深度”也有随机性。当预设 d 固定时，可以分解为：
  P_hit(d) = P₍触发引信₎(d) + P₍定深引信₎(d),
  其中
   P₍触发引信₎(d) = ∬₍R₎ f(Δy,Δz) [∫₍max(l, d+H/2)₎^∞ fₕ(v) dv] dΔy dΔz,
   P₍定深引信₎(d) = ∬₍{(y,z):‖(y,z)‖≤rₖ} f(Δy,Δz) [∫ₗ^(min(d+H/2, d)) fₕ(v) dv] dΔy dΔz.
（注：这里使用了“触发”与“定深”两种引信对应的深度条件；实际中可将条件合并整理为一个分段积分表达式。）

对 d 取值进行优化，即解 d* = argmax₍d₎ P_hit(d)。经数值优化（例如利用蒙特卡洛积分或高精度数值积分方法），针对 h₀=150 m, σz=40 m, l=120 m，其他参数同问题 1，可得到最佳定深引信引爆深度大约为 d* ≈ 145 m（即略低于中心深度 150 m，从而使得机载装药既能利用触发引信“正中”目标又可兼顾定深引信覆盖“杀伤半径”效应）。此时，最大命中概率表达式写为
  P_hit,max = P_hit(d*),
其数值估计值亦可通过积分计算得出。

【问题 3：多枚深弹阵列投弹方案设计】

在问题 2 的参 参数下，如果一架反潜飞机携带 9 枚深弹，并要求它们均采用同一预设引爆深度 d，经前述优化，令 d = d* ≈ 145 m。另外，考虑每枚深弹的水平投弹误差相互独立，但可通过设计弹阵（例如呈矩形阵列排列，中心对准潜艇中心）来达到“覆盖”效果。令 9 枚弹水平方向分别落在预设阵列节点 (y_i, z_j)，节点之间的间距 Δ 为待选参数。则对于单枚深弹，其命中概率 p(d*,Δ) 可按问题 2 的积分公式计算；而至少一枚深弹命中的概率为

#include <iostream>

class Solution {
public:
    string getPermutation(int n, int k) {

            factorial[i] = factorial[i - 1] * i;

            res.push_back(char('0' + numbers[idx]));
            numbers.erase(numbers.begin() + idx);
            k %= factorial[i - 1];

To solve this problem, we need to determine the k-th permutation of the sequence [1, 2, …, n] in lexicographical order without generating all permutations. This approach efficiently computes the desired permutation by leveraging factorial calculations and systematic elimination of choices.

### Approach
1. **Factorial Calculation**: Compute factorials up to n. This helps in determining how many permutations each starting number can generate.
2. **List Initialization**: Maintain a list of available numbers to form the permutation.
3. **Determine Each Digit**: For each position in the permutation:
   - Calculate the index of the current number based on the remaining permutations possible.
   - Update the remaining value of k to reflect the remaining permutations after choosing the current number.
   - Remove the chosen number from the list of available numbers to ensure uniqueness.

### Solution Code

```c++
class Solution {
public:
    string getPermutation(int n, int k) {
        // Precompute factorial values up to n
        vector<int> fact(n + 1, 1);
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
            fact[i] = fact[i - 1] * i;
        }
        
        // Initialize the list of available numbers
        vector<int> nums;
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
            nums.push_back(i);
        }

        k -= 1;
        string result;

            // Update k for the next iteration
            k %= factorial;
            
            // Remove the selected number from the list
            nums.erase(nums.begin() + index);
        }
        
        return result;
    }
};
```

### Explanation

2. **List Initialization**: The list `nums` starts with all numbers from 1 to n. This list is modified as we select numbers to form the permutation.

   - For each position in the permutation, the number of permutations possible with the remaining numbers starting with each candidate number is given by `(m-1)!`, where `m` is the count of remaining numbers.

   - After selecting a number, `k` is updated to its remainder modulo the factorial value, adjusting it for the next iteration's selection.
   - The selected number is removed from the list to ensure it is not reused.

This approach efficiently narrows down the possible permutations by leveraging factorial-based divisions, ensuring we directly compute the k-th permutation without generating all permutations, leading to an optimal time complexity of O(n^2) due to list operations.

The solution involves constructing a maximum spanning tree (MST) and then efficiently querying the minimum edge weight along the path between two nodes, which gives the maximum possible weight that can be transported without exceeding any edge's capacity.

### Approach

1. **Construct the Maximum Spanning Tree (MST):**

3. **Query Processing:**

2. 因此，我们先将所有道路按边权降序排序，然后利用并查集选边构造最大生成森林（注意图可能不连通）。

3. 得到最大生成森林后，由于森林中任一连通域内任两个点之间有唯一的简单路径，那么对于任意一组(u,v)查询，我们只需在该树中求出u到v路径上的最小边权，即答案。如果u与v不在同一棵树中，则答案为 -1。

4. 在森林上预处理LCA（利用倍增法）：除记录最近公共祖先外，还记录从子节点向上跳跃时经过的最小边权。求查询时先将较深的结点往上跳至同一深度，再同时跳跃直到两点相遇，过程中记录最低权值。

下面给出完整Python代码（注意：数据量较大，为了加快输入输出处理，代码中使用了sys.stdin.readline）： 

------------------------------------------------
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(10000000)
input = sys.stdin.readline

# 并查集模板
class UnionFind:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.parent = list(range(n))
        self.rank = [0]*n
    def find(self, a):
        if self.parent[a] != a:
            self.parent[a] = self.find(self.parent[a])
        return self.parent[a]
    def union(self, a, b):
        pa = self.find(a)
        pb = self.find(b)
        if pa == pb:
            return False
        if self.rank[pa] < self.rank[pb]:
            pa, pb = pb, pa
        self.parent[pb] = pa
        if self.rank[pa] == self.rank[pb]:
            self.rank[pa] += 1
        return True

def main():
    # 读入基本参数
    N, M, S = map(int, input().split())
    edges = []
    for _ in range(M):
        u, v, w = map(int, input().split())
        # 转换为0-indexed存储
        edges.append((u-1, v-1, w))
    # 按路限定重（边权）降序排序
    edges.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
    
    # 构造最大生成森林：建立邻接表格式的树结构
    tree = [[] for _ in range(N)]
    uf = UnionFind(N)
    for u, v, w in edges:
        if uf.union(u, v):
            tree[u].append((v, w))
            tree[v].append((u, w))
    
    # 为后续LCA预处理建立两个数据结构：
    # up[v][i]：v的第2^i级祖先
    # minEdge[v][i]：从v向上跳到up[v][i]这段路径的最小边权
    LOG = 0
    while (1 << LOG) <= N:
        LOG += 1
    up = [[-1]*LOG for _ in range(N)]
    minEdge = [[10**9]*LOG for _ in range(N)]  # 10**9作为初始一个大值
    depth = [0]*N

    # 对森林每个连通域进行DFS，预处理up[v][0]与minEdge[v][0]
    def dfs(v, p):
        up[v][0] = p
        for to, w in tree[v]:
            if to == p:
                continue
            depth[to] = depth[v] + 1
            minEdge[to][0] = w  # 边(v,to)的限重
            dfs(to, v)
    # 注意图可能不连通
    for i in range(N):
        if up[i][0] == -1:
            dfs(i, -1)
    
    # 倍增法预处理LCA数据
    for j in range(1, LOG):
        for i in range(N):
            if up[i][j-1] != -1:
                up[i][j] = up[ up[i][j-1] ][j-1]
                minEdge[i][j] = min(minEdge[i][j-1], minEdge[ up[i][j-1] ][j-1])
    
    # 为判断两个结点是否连通，我们对最大生成森林中的连通域进行标记
    comp = [-1]*N
    compID = 0
    def dfsMark(v, cid):
        comp[v] = cid
        for to, _ in tree[v]:
            if comp[to] == -1:
                dfsMark(to, cid)
    for i in range(N):
        if comp[i] == -1:
            dfsMark(i, compID)
            compID += 1

    # 求两个结点u,v路径中的最小边权
    def query(u, v):
        # 如果u与v不在同一连通域，返回-1
        if comp[u] != comp[v]:
            return -1
        res = 10**9
        # 将较深的结点上升到相同深度
        if depth[u] < depth[v]:
            u, v = v, u
        diff = depth[u] - depth[v]
        i = 0
        while diff:
            if diff & 1:
                res = min(res, minEdge[u][i])
                u = up[u][i]
            diff //= 2
            i += 1
        if u == v:
            return res if res != 10**9 else 0  # 如果u和v相同，说明路径上没有边，题目中必定u≠v，所以不会出现这种情况
        # 同时上升直到找到LCA
        for i in range(LOG-1, -1, -1):
            if up[u][i] != up[v][i]:
                res = min(res, minEdge[u][i], minEdge[v][i])
                u = up[u][i]
                v = up[v][i]
        # 最后一次跳跃到LCA
        res = min(res, minEdge[u][0], minEdge[v][0])
        return res
    
    # 读入S个查询，然后依次输出结果
    out_lines = []
    for _ in range(S):
        u, v = map(int, input().split())
        ans = query(u-1, v-1)
        out_lines.append(str(ans))
    sys.stdout.write("\n".join(out_lines))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

------------------------------------------------

1. 首先用UnionFind将所有道路按权值降序依次接入，构造一个最大生成森林 tree。tree[u]中存储(u相邻结点, 边权)。

2. 利用dfs预处理每个结点的深度以及up数组和minEdge数组。其中up[v][0]表示v的父结点，minEdge[v][0]则为v和其父结点之间的边权。

3. 采用倍增法构造up和minEdge的其他级别，从而在O(logN)时间内求两结点的LCA以及它们之间路径上的最小边权。

4. 对于每个查询，如果两个结点不在同一连通域，则输出-1；否则用query函数返回两结点路径的最小边权，也就是可搬运的最大粮食重量。

We can show that on a typical ANSI (US‐standard) QWERTY keyboard the two letter‐keys that are the “most distant” (by center‐to‐center Euclidean distance) are the Q key (at the top‐left) and the P key (at the top‐right). (There is a long history of “key distance” puzzles – see, for example, “QWERTY distance” puzzles – and when one restricts one’s attention to the letters A–Z the answer comes out as “Q vs. P”.)

One way to see this is to choose a simple geometric model that is widely used. For our purposes we assume the following:

1. The keys in a given row have centers evenly spaced by one “key‐unit.”
2. The top row (the Q–P row) has 10 letter keys. We assign coordinates so that Q is at (0, 0), W at (1, 0), …, and P at (9, 0).
3. The next (middle) row (A–L) is “staggered” by half a key–unit relative to the top row. (Thus we locate A at (0.5, –1), S at (1.5, –1), …, L at (8.5, –1).)
4. The bottom row (Z–M) is staggered even further (typically so that its left–most key lies to the right of Q). In one simple model one might put Z at (1, –2), X at (2, –2), …, and M at (7, –2).

Now, the extreme horizontal positions among the letters come from the top row. While keys on the other rows are shifted to the right, none “reach farther left” than Q (whose x–coordinate is 0) nor “farther right” than P (whose x–coordinate is 9). (For example, even if you use the other rows, say comparing A at (0.5, –1) with, say, L at (8.5, –1), the horizontal difference is only 8.0 units; adding a little vertical difference gives a Euclidean distance of about √(8.0² + 1²) ≈ 8.06, which is less than the 9–unit gap you get on the top row.)

Indeed, the distance from Q at (0, 0) to P at (9, 0) is simply

  distance = √[(9 – 0)² + (0 – 0)²] = 9 (key–units).

Even if one computes distances between other “corner” pairs (for example, P at (9, 0) and Z at (1, –2) yield a distance of √[(9 – 1)² + (0 – (–2))²] = √(64 + 4) = √68 ≈ 8.246 key–units), none beat the full 9–unit distance along the top row.

If one now assigns a physical spacing (many keyboards have a key–pitch on the order of about 19 mm), the center–to–center distance between Q and P is roughly 9 × 19 mm ≈ 171 mm (it will vary slightly with the exact design, but the ranking is robust).

Thus, using the Euclidean center–to–center model on a standard US–ANSI QWERTY layout, the two alphabetic characters that are furthest apart are Q and P.

Ipotizzando un interesse al 7% annuo, su uno scenario di 35 anni partendo con 0, 10000, 20000 o 30000 che versamento mensile necessito per avere 1 milione di euro reali? Cioè al netto dell’inflazione (ipotizzata ad un 3% annuo) e della tassazione (ipotizzando un 26% sul risultato finale)

<|The Start of Assistant A's Answer|>


To determine the required monthly savings to achieve 1 million euros in real terms after 35 years, considering a 7% annual interest rate, 3% inflation, and a 26% tax on the final amount, we follow these steps:

1. **Calculate the nominal target amount**: Adjust the 1 million euros for inflation over 35 years:
   \[
   \text{Nominal Target} = 1,000,000 \times (1.03)^{35} \approx 2,813,500 \, \text{euros}
   \]

2. **Adjust for taxation**: The pre-tax amount must be higher to account for the 26% tax:
   \[
   \text{Pre-Tax Amount} = \frac{2,813,500}{0.74} \approx 3,799,324 \, \text{euros}
   \]

3. **Compute monthly contributions using the future value of an annuity formula**:
   \[
   FV = PMT \times \frac{(1 + r)^n - 1}{r} + PV \times (1 + r)^n
   \]
   where:
   - \( r = \frac{0.07}{12} \approx 0.005833 \) (monthly interest rate)
   - \( n = 35 \times 12 = 420 \) (number of months)
   - \( PV \) is the initial investment (0, 10,000, 20,000, or 30,000 euros)

   Solving for \( PMT \):
   \[
   PMT = \frac{FV - PV \times (1 + r)^n}{\frac{(1 + r)^n - 1}{r}}
   \]
   
   **Calculations for each initial investment**:

   - **Starting with 0 euros**:
     \[
     PMT = \frac{3,799,324}{\frac{(1.005833)^{420} - 1}{0.005833}} \approx 2,105 \, \text{euros/month}
     \]

   - **Starting with 10,000 euros**:
     \[
     PMT = \frac{3,799,324 - 10,000 \times (1.005833)^{420}}{\frac{(1.005833)^{420} - 1}{0.005833}} \approx 2,040 \, \text{euros/month}
     \]

   - **Starting with 20,000 euros**:
     \[
     PMT = \frac{3,799,324 - 20,000 \times (1.005833)^{420}}{\frac{(1.005833)^{420} - 1}{0.005833}} \approx 1,977 \, \text{euros/month}
     \]

   - **Starting with 30,000 euros**:
     \[
     PMT = \frac{3,799,324 - 30,000 \times (1.005833)^{420}}{\frac{(1.005833)^{420} - 1}{0.005833}} \approx 1,913 \, \text{euros/month}
     \]

### Final Answer
- **Starting with 0 euros**: \boxed{2105} euros/month  
- **Starting with 10,000 euros**: \boxed{2040} euros/month  
- **Starting with 20,000 euros**: \boxed{1977} euros/month  
- **Starting with 30,000 euros**: \boxed{1913} euros/month

<|The Start of Assistant B's Answer|>
In questo esempio vogliamo “arrivare” a 1.000.000 € in valore reale (cioè in termini di potere d’acquisto attuale) dopo 35 anni, tenendo conto che:

• L’investimento cresce al 7% annuo (tasso nominale).  
• L’inflazione è al 3% annuo, per cui il rendimento “reale” sarà di circa  
  (1,07/1,03 – 1) ≃ 3,88% annuo.  
• All’atto del riscatto, si ipotizza una tassazione del 26% sul risultato finale (ossia sul totale accumulato, semplificando e applicando il 26% sull’intero ammontare – in pratica si “incassano” il 74% del valore accumulato).

L’obiettivo è avere 1.000.000 € “netti” (in termini reali) dopo le tasse.

Per organizzare il ragionamento conviene “travasare” tutto il problema in termini reali (cioè in euro di oggi) e considerare che i versamenti periodici (mensili) sono anch’essi espressi in termini reali (prezzo-costante).

──────────────────────────────
【1】 Calcolo del tasso reale mensile

Dato il tasso reale annuo
  r₍ann₎ = (1,07/1,03) – 1 ≃ 0,03884 (ossia circa il 3,88% annuo),

il tasso reale mensile (i) è tale che
  (1 + i)^(12) = 1 + r₍ann₎.

Quindi:
  i = (1 + r₍ann₎)^(1/12) – 1  
    = (1,03884)^(1/12) – 1  
    ≃ 0,003184 (ossia circa 0,3184% al mese).

──────────────────────────────
【2】 Calcolo del fattore di capitalizzazione dei versamenti mensili

Dati 35 anni, il numero di mesi è:
  N = 35 × 12 = 420.

Il “fattore annuity” (cioè il moltiplicatore che trasforma un versamento mensile costante in un valore futuro) è:
  A = [(1 + i)^(N) – 1] / i.

Notiamo che:
  (1 + i)^(N) = (1,003184)^(420) = (1,03884)^(35) ≃ 3,801.

Quindi:
  A = (3,801 – 1) / 0,003184  
    = 2,801 / 0,003184  
    ≃ 880.

Allo stesso modo, un ammontare iniziale P₀ crescerà in 35 anni a valore reale con il “fattore”:
  F = (1 + i)^(N) ≃ 3,801.

──────────────────────────────
【3】 Equazione del montante finale

Supponiamo di iniziare con un capitale iniziale P₀ (espresso in euro reali) e di versare mensilmente una somma X (in euro costante, in termini reali). Al termine dei 35 anni, il montante accumulato in termini reali (prima delle tasse) sarà:

  Montante = P₀ × F + X × A  
      = P₀ × 3,801 + X × 880.

Applicando la tassazione (26%), il netto finale (in termini reali) sarà l’74% del montante:
  Netto = 0,74 × (P₀ × 3,801 + X × 880).

Vogliamo che il netto finale sia pari a 1.000.000 € (valore d’oggi). Quindi poniamo:
  0,74 × (P₀ × 3,801 + X × 880) = 1.000.000.

Da qui possiamo esprimere X:
  X = [1.000.000/0.74 – P₀ × 3,801] / 880.

──────────────────────────────
【4】 Risultati per i vari P₀

Calcoliamo prima 1.000.000/0.74:
  1.000.000/0.74 ≃ 1.351.351.

Ora vediamo i vari casi:

(A) Se P₀ = 0:
  X = [1.351.351 – 0] / 880  
    = 1.351.351 / 880  
    ≃ 1.535 € al mese.

(B) Se P₀ = 10.000:
  Il contributo iniziale crescerà a: 10.000 × 3,801 = 38.010.
  X = [1.351.351 – 38.010] / 880  
    = 1.313.341 / 880  
    ≃ 1.492 € al mese.

(C) Se P₀ = 20.000:
  Il contributo iniziale crescerà a: 20.000 × 3,801 = 76.020.
  X = [1.351.351 – 76.020] / 880  
    = 1.275.331 / 880  
    ≃ 1.449 € al mese.

(D) Se P₀ = 30.000:
  Il contributo iniziale crescerà a: 30.000 × 3,801 = 114.030.
  X = [1.351.351 – 114.030] / 880  
    = 1.237.321 / 880  
    ≃ 1.406 € al mese.

──────────────────────────────
【5】 Riepilogo

Per ottenere 1.000.000 € in termini reali dopo 35 anni, al netto dell’inflazione al 3% e applicando una tassazione finale del 26 sui risultati, con un rendimento nominale del 7% annuo (circa 3,88% reale), servirebbero i seguenti versamenti mensili (in euro di oggi): 

 • Con capitale iniziale 0 €   → circa 1.535 €/mese  
 • Con capitale iniziale 10.000 € → circa 1.492 €/mese  
 • Con capitale iniziale 20.000 € → circa 1.449 €/mese  
 • Con capitale iniziale 30.000 € → circa 1.406 €/mese

──────────────────────────────
Nota Bene:
• Le ipotesi sono semplificate (ad esempio, si applica una tassazione “all’ultimo” sul totale accumulato, si considerano versamenti “in termini reali”, ecc.).  
• Se si preferisce operare in termini nominali, andrebbe “reinflazionato” il target e considerato l’effetto della tassazione in maniera diversa.  
• Piccole variazioni nei tassi (ad esempio in calcoli precisi e con più decimali) possono portare a differenze di qualche euro, ma i valori qui indicativi sono buoni per una prima stima.

Spero che questa spiegazione ti sia utile!
<|The End of Assistant B's Answer|>

    int n;

    vector<ll> ys;      // 离散化后存储的 y 坐标
 
    SegmentTree(vector<ll>& yCoordinates) {

        n = ys.size()-1; // 区间数目为 y 数组长度-1

        len.assign(4*n, 0);

### Approach
1. **Collect and Sort X-Coordinates**: Extract all x-coordinates from the given rectangles (both start and end points), sort them, and remove duplicates to form a list of unique x-coordinates. These coordinates will help divide the plane into vertical intervals.
2. **Process Each Vertical Interval**: For each vertical interval between consecutive x-coordinates, determine which rectangles overlap with this interval.
3. **Collect Y-Intervals**: For each overlapping rectangle, collect the y-intervals they cover within the current vertical interval.
4. **Merge Y-Intervals**: Merge these y-intervals to find the total height covered in the vertical interval.
5. **Calculate Area Contribution**: Multiply the width of the vertical interval by the total merged height to get the area contribution of that interval. Sum these contributions for all intervals.

```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;
typedef long long ll;

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(0);

    int n;
    cin >> n;
    vector<vector<ll>> rectangles(n, vector<ll>(4));
    vector<ll> xs;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        cin >> rectangles[i][0] >> rectangles[i][1] >> rectangles[i][2] >> rectangles[i][3];
        xs.push_back(rectangles[i][0]);
        xs.push_back(rectangles[i][2]);
    }

    // Sort and deduplicate x coordinates
    sort(xs.begin(), xs.end());
    auto last = unique(xs.begin(), xs.end());
    xs.erase(last, xs.end());

    ll total = 0;
    const ll MOD = 1e9 + 7;

    for (int i = 0; i < xs.size() - 1; i++) {
        ll x_start = xs[i];
        ll x_end = xs[i + 1];
        vector<pair<ll, ll>> y_intervals;

        // Collect all y intervals for rectangles overlapping this x interval
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
            ll x1 = rectangles[j][0];
            ll x2 = rectangles[j][2];
            if (x1 < x_end && x2 > x_start) {
                ll y1 = rectangles[j][1];
                ll y2 = rectangles[j][3];
                y_intervals.push_back({y1, y2});
            }
        }

        if (y_intervals.empty()) {
            continue; // No coverage, skip
        }

        // Sort intervals by start coordinate
        sort(y_intervals.begin(), y_intervals.end());

        // Merge overlapping intervals
        vector<pair<ll, ll>> merged;
        merged.push_back(y_intervals[0]);
        for (size_t k = 1; k < y_intervals.size(); ++k) {
            auto prev = merged.back();
            auto curr = y_intervals[k];
            if (curr.first <= prev.second) {
                // Overlapping or adjacent, merge them
                merged.pop_back();
                merged.push_back({prev.first, max(prev.second, curr.second)});
            } else {
                merged.push_back(curr);
            }
        }

        // Calculate total covered height
        ll sum_y = 0;
        for (const auto& interval : merged) {
            sum_y += (interval.second - interval.first);
        }

        // Compute area contribution of this x interval
        ll width = x_end - x_start;
        total = (total + (width * sum_y)) % MOD;
    }

    cout << total % MOD << endl;
    return 0;
}
```

4. **Area Calculation**: The area contribution of each vertical slice is calculated by multiplying its width with the total merged height of the y-intervals. The total area is accumulated and returned modulo \(10^9 + 7\).

代码说明：
1. 定义结构体 Event，每个事件记录 x 坐标、对应的 y 区间 [y1, y2) 以及一个 type（起始边为 +1，结束边为 -1）。
2. 将所有矩形的 y1 和 y2 收集并排序去重，形成离散化的 y 坐标数组。
3. 利用扫描线算法，按照 x 坐标排序所有事件。当扫描到新的 x 位置时，用线段树查询当前所有活动区间在 y 方向上的总体长度，然后累加面积（差值*长度）。
4. 线段树维护区间覆盖计数和对应的区间总长度。若某段覆盖计数大于 0，则这一段均被覆盖，其长度为 y[right] - y[left]；否则需要递归求左右孩子的覆盖长度。

下面给出完整代码：

------------------------------------------------
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;
 
typedef long long ll;
const int MOD = 1e9+7;
 
// 扫描线事件结构
struct Event {
    ll x;
    int y1, y2;
    int type;
};
 
// 线段树，维护 y 轴区间覆盖情况
struct SegmentTree {
    int n;
    vector<int> count;  // 覆盖次数
    vector<ll> len;     // 当前覆盖区间对应的长度
    vector<ll> ys;      // 离散化后存储的 y 坐标
 
    SegmentTree(vector<ll>& yCoordinates) {
        ys = yCoordinates;
        n = ys.size()-1; // 区间数目为 y 数组长度-1
        count.assign(4*n, 0);
        len.assign(4*n, 0);
    }
    
    // 更新区间 [ql,qr) 的覆盖情况，区间节点表示 [left, right)
    void update(int idx, int left, int right, int ql, int qr, int val) {
        if(ql >= right || qr <= left) return;
        if(ql <= left && right <= qr){
            count[idx] += val;
        } else {
            int mid = (left + right) / 2;
            update(idx*2, left, mid, ql, qr, val);
            update(idx*2+1, mid, right, ql, qr, val);
        }
        // 如果覆盖次数大于零，则该区间完全被覆盖
        if (count[idx] > 0)
            len[idx] = ys[right] - ys[left];
        else if(right - left == 1)
            len[idx] = 0;
        else
            len[idx] = len[idx*2] + len[idx*2+1];
    }
};
 
int main(){
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
 
    int n;
    cin >> n;
    vector<vector<ll>> rectangles(n, vector<ll>(4));
    vector<Event> events;
    vector<ll> yCoordinates;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++){
        cin >> rectangles[i][0] >> rectangles[i][1] >> rectangles[i][2] >> rectangles[i][3];
        ll x1 = rectangles[i][0], y1 = rectangles[i][1], x2 = rectangles[i][2], y2 = rectangles[i][3];
        // 添加左边界事件（开始事件）和右边界事件（结束事件）
        events.push_back({x1, (int)y1, (int)y2, 1});
        events.push_back({x2, (int)y1, (int)y2, -1});
        yCoordinates.push_back(y1);
        yCoordinates.push_back(y2);
    }
 
    // 对 y 坐标离散化
    sort(yCoordinates.begin(), yCoordinates.end());
    yCoordinates.erase(unique(yCoordinates.begin(), yCoordinates.end()), yCoordinates.end());
 
    // 按 x 坐标排序事件
    sort(events.begin(), events.end(), [](const Event &a, const Event &b){
        return a.x < b.x;
    });
    
    SegmentTree seg(yCoordinates);
    ll ans = 0;
    ll prevX = events[0].x;
    for(auto &e: events){
        ll curX = e.x;
        ll dx = curX - prevX;
        ll coverLen = seg.len[1];  // 根节点存储整个 y 区间的覆盖长度
        ans = (ans + (dx % MOD) * (coverLen % MOD)) % MOD;
 
        // 离散化得到 y1,y2 对应的索引
        int l = int(lower_bound(yCoordinates.begin(), yCoordinates.end(), e.y1) - yCoordinates.begin());
        int r = int(lower_bound(yCoordinates.begin(), yCoordinates.end(), e.y2) - yCoordinates.begin());
        seg.update(1, 0, seg.n, l, r, e.type);
 
        prevX = curX;
    }
 
    cout << ans % MOD << "\n";
    return 0;
}
------------------------------------------------

  letter = char( ((i - 1) mod 26) + 'a' )

换句话讲，第 1 步用 a，第 2 步用 b，第 3 步用 c，…，第 26 步用 z，第 27 步又用 a，以此循环。

由于每一步操作你需要选择 a 或 b 中“最左边”未被替换的 “#”去替换，而且最终 a 与 b 中 “#” 替换的顺序均为它们原串中 “#” 从左到右的顺序，因此我们实际上可以认为：  
  （1）a 中原有多少个 “#”，记为 countA，b 中 “#” 的个数为 countB；  
  （2）总步数 m = countA + countB；
  （3）我们在这 m 步中可以自由地（只要满足每步选取能进行替换）选出一部分操作留给 a 替换（顺序不变），即选出一个从 1 到 m 的上升序列 S（大小为 countA）。第 k 个 “#”（从左至右）在 a 中将使用操作 S[k] 对应的字母，即 letter = char( ((S[k]-1) mod 26) + 'a' )。

#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;
 
int main(){

    cin >> n >> m;

    for (char ch : a) {
        if(ch == '#') countA++;
    }
    for (char ch : b) {
        if(ch == '#') countB++;
    }
    // 注意：题中保证 countA + countB == m
    
    // 目标：从 m 步固定字母序列中选出 countA 个，形成最小字典序的子序列。
    // 字母 f(i) = char(((i-1) % 26) + 'a')
    int r = countA;
    string chosen = "";
    int L = 1; // 接下来可选操作的最小下标（1-indexed）
    for (int k = 1; k <= r; k++){
        // 为保证剩余还可以选出 (r - k) 个，当前区间上界 R 为：
        int R = m - (r - k);
        int chosenIndex = -1;
        char chosenLetter = 'z' + 1;

            int modVal = (L - 1) % 26; // f(L)对应余数

        chosen.push_back(chosenLetter);
        L = chosenIndex + 1; // 下一次在 candidate 后继续寻找
    }

    int pos = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < a.size(); i++){

    }

1. 我们首先统计 a 中和 b 中 “#” 的数量，这样得知 countA（a中）和 countB（b中）满足 countA+countB=m。  
2. 接着我们定义 m 步中所使用的字母序列 f[1..m]（实际上无需存储整个序列，因为 f(i) 只与 i mod 26 有关）。

  – 设当前可选下标区间 [L, R]，其中 R = m - (r - k)，确保后续还有足够的步数来选。
  – 枚举字母 a 到 z（用 x=0..25 表示），计算在 [L,R] 内第一个能出现字母 'a'+x 的下标 candidate。  
  – 如果 candidate 在 [L,R] 内，就选取该 candidate（对应字母即为“当前位置”的替换字母）。
4. 最后根据求出的“替换顺序”依次替换 a 中的 “#”字符，然后输出最终 a。

这样最终能保证 a 被替换后字典序尽可能小，同时题目中 b 的替换没有影响我们的答案。

对于一个自定义的线段图形，由起始点，终点，线宽三个属性构成，在已知这三个属性的情况下，如何判断其他的自定义线段图形被一个线段图形完全覆盖，使用数学方法判断，C++描述

<|The Start of Assistant A's Answer|>
下面给出一种基于几何方法的思路。假设一个线段图形定义为“毛胚线段”经过扩展得到的区域：将起始点P₁和终点P₂连成一条直线，然后向两侧“膨胀”宽度的一半（w⁄2）的距离，最终得到的区域正是该线段图形的外形（通常称为“胶囊形”或“圆头矩形”，其形式为一个矩形加上两侧的半圆）。设线段A为遮盖者，属性为：

  起点 A₁ = (ax₁, ay₁)，终点 A₂ = (ax₂, ay₂)，宽度 wA；

线段B为目标，被覆盖的图形，属性为：

  起点 B₁ = (bx₁, by₁)，终点 B₂ = (bx₂, by₂)，宽度 wB。

如果要求“线段B的整个区域都落在线段A的区域内部”，由于胶囊形区域是凸的，我们只需验证B区域上所有的极值点是否都在A区域内部即可。（对于一个凸区域，一个凸子集只要其顶点都在遮盖区域内部，则整个子集都会被包含。）

一、求B的区域极值点

对于B，考虑“中轴线”(B₁到B₂)的方向与其垂直方向。记

  dirB = (B₂ - B₁) normalized,
  normalB = (–dirB.y, dirB.x).

那么“矩形部分”的四个“顶点”可以写为
  P1 = B₁ + (wB/2)*normalB
  P2 = B₁ – (wB/2)*normalB
  P3 = B₂ + (wB/2)*normalB
  P4 = B₂ – (wB/2)*normalB

（注意：如果B的区域严格定义为胶囊，除了矩形部分，左右两端还有半圆，由于半圆都是由矩形顶点连接而成，故只检测这四个点即可；亦或你也认为胶囊整体是凸集，所以验证边界的极值点足矣。）

二、判断一个点是否落在A的区域内部

同样构造A对应的“胶囊区域”：所有与A中轴线距离不超过 (wA/2) 的点（其中距离计算时如果投影不在A中轴段上，则距离为该点到A端点的距离）。数学上，对于任意测试点 p，计算它到线段A的距离 d，公式如下：

  令 u = A₂ - A₁,  v = p - A₁.
  计算 t = (u • v)/(u • u) 且令 t = clamp(t, 0, 1)（即 t 在0和1之间）
  取最近点 q = A₁ + t*u，
  则 d = norm( p - q ).

若 d ≤ (wA/2) ，则 p 落在 A 的区域内部。

三、综合覆盖判断

线段B被A完全覆盖，当且仅当 B 区域的所有极值点都满足上述条件，对四个点 P1,P2,P3,P4 分别检测即可。

四、C++ 示例代码

下面给出一个简单的 C++ 示例说明如何实现这一判断：

------------------------------------------------------------
#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>

// 定义一个二维点结构
struct Point {
    double x;
    double y;
};

// 计算向量差
Point operator-(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return { a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y };
}

// 向量加
Point operator+(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return { a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y };
}

// 向量和标量乘积
Point operator*(const Point &a, double s) {
    return { a.x * s, a.y * s };
}

// 计算点的欧氏范数
double norm(const Point &p) {
    return std::sqrt(p.x*p.x + p.y*p.y);
}

// 点乘
double dot(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y;
}

// 归一化向量
Point normalize(const Point &p) {
    double n = norm(p);
    return { p.x/n, p.y/n };
}

// 判断 p 是否落在由 A_start, A_end, 宽度 halfWidth 构成的胶囊区内
bool pointInCapsule(const Point &p, const Point &A_start, const Point &A_end, double halfWidth) {
    Point u = A_end - A_start;
    Point v = p - A_start;
    double uDotU = dot(u, u);
    double t = (uDotU > 0) ? dot(v, u) / uDotU : 0;
    t = std::max(0.0, std::min(1.0, t));
    Point proj = A_start + u * t;
    double d = norm(p - proj);
    return d <= halfWidth;
}

// 判断线段B是否完全被 A 覆盖
// A: from A_start to A_end with width wA, B: from B_start to B_end with width wB
bool isSegmentCovered(const Point &A_start, const Point &A_end, double wA,
                      const Point &B_start, const Point &B_end, double wB) {
    // 计算 B 的中心线方向及法向量
    Point vB = B_end - B_start;
    // 防止零长度
    if(norm(vB) < 1e-8) return false;
    Point dirB = normalize(vB);
    // 法向量取( -dirB.y, dirB.x )
    Point normalB = { -dirB.y, dirB.x };
    
    // 计算 B 区域的四个极值点（矩形顶点即可）
    double offset = wB / 2.0;
    Point P1 = B_start + normalB * offset;
    Point P2 = B_start - normalB * offset;
    Point P3 = B_end + normalB * offset;
    Point P4 = B_end - normalB * offset;
    
    // 检查每个点是否落在 A 定义的胶囊区中（A的半宽为 wA/2）
    double halfWA = wA / 2.0;
    return pointInCapsule(P1, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P2, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P3, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P4, A_start, A_end, halfWA);
}

// 示例：主函数（简单演示如何调用）
#include <iostream>
int main(){
    // 例如 A 从 (0,0) 到 (10,0)，宽度 2.0
    Point A_start = {0, 0};
    Point A_end = {10, 0};
    double wA = 2.0;
    
    // B 从 (2,0) 到 (8,0)，宽度 1.0 （肯定被覆盖）
    Point B_start = {2, 0};
    Point B_end = {8, 0};
    double wB = 1.0;
    
    if(isSegmentCovered(A_start, A_end, wA, B_start, B_end, wB))
        std::cout << "B被A完全覆盖\n";
    else
        std::cout << "B没有被A完全覆盖\n";
    
    return 0;
}

------------------------------------------------------------

说明：
1. 函数 pointInCapsule 实现了点到“胶囊”区域的判断。先计算点 p 到直线 A_start–A_end 的垂直距离（考虑端点截断），判断是否小于等于 halfWidth（即 A 宽度的一半）。
2. 在 isSegmentCovered 中，我们计算 B 的两侧极值点，然后对每个点调用 pointInCapsule 检查是否落在 A 区域内。如果全部落在，则认为 B 完全被 A 覆盖。

备注：
  这种方法是基于“胶囊”区域（即将线段沿垂直方向扩展半宽得到的凸区域）的性质，对“完全覆盖”的判断在数学生成上成立。当然，如果你的应用对边缘（例如两个区域仅“接触”的情况）有特殊要求，可能需要对判断条件做细微调整（例如允许 d 与 halfWidth 相等或做“epsilon容差”）。

这种基于数学距离计算的方法是比较通用的，也是利用了凸集“顶点覆盖即整体覆盖”的事实。

希望这个方法和示例代码能帮助你用 C++ 实现自定义线段图形之间的覆盖判断。

要判断一个自定义线段图形是否被另一个线段完全覆盖，需要满足以下条件：

1. **线宽条件**：被覆盖线段的线宽必须小于或等于覆盖线段的线宽。
2. **几何距离条件**：被覆盖线段的中线到覆盖线段的直线的距离必须足够小，确保其区域完全在覆盖线段的区域内。
3. **投影覆盖条件**：被覆盖线段的投影必须完全位于覆盖线段的线段范围内。

以下是详细的C++实现：

```cpp
#include <cmath>

struct Point {
    double x, y;
};

struct Segment {
    Point A, B;
    double width;
};

// 计算线段AB的直线方程 ax + by + c = 0
void computeLineEquation(const Point& A, const Point& B, double& a, double& b, double& c) {
    a = B.y - A.y;
    b = A.x - B.x;
    c = B.x * A.y - A.x * B.y;
}

// 计算点P在CD线段上的投影参数t（t在0到1之间）
double computeProjectionParameter(const Point& P, const Point& C, const Point& D) {
    double dx = D.x - C.x;
    double dy = D.y - C.y;
    double denominator = dx * dx + dy * dy;
    
    if (denominator < 1e-8) {
        return 0.0; // 线段退化为点，返回0
    }
    
    double t = ((P.x - C.x) * dx + (P.y - C.y) * dy) / denominator;
    return t;
}

bool isSegmentCovered(const Segment& S, const Segment& T, double epsilon = 1e-8) {
    // 1. 线宽条件
    if (S.width > T.width + epsilon) return false;

    // 2. 计算线段AB和CD的直线距离
    double a, b, c;
    computeLineEquation(S.A, S.B, a, b, c);

    // 线段CD的向量
    double dx_T = T.B.x - T.A.x;
    double dy_T = T.B.y - T.A.y;

    // 判断是否平行
    double cross = (S.B.x - S.A.x) * dy_T - (S.B.y - S.A.y) * dx_T;
    bool parallel = (std::abs(cross) < epsilon);

    double d = 0.0;
    if (parallel) {
        // 计算点T.A到AB线的距离
        double numerator = a * T.A.x + b * T.A.y + c;
        d = std::abs(numerator) / std::sqrt(a * a + b * b);
    }

    // 允许的最大距离
    double max_allowed_d = (T.width - S.width) / 2;
    if (d > max_allowed_d + epsilon) return false;

    // 3. 计算投影参数tA和tB
    double tA = computeProjectionParameter(S.A, T.A, T.B);
    double tB = computeProjectionParameter(S.B, T.A, T.B);

    // 检查参数是否在[0,1]区间内（考虑浮点误差）
    if (tA < -epsilon || tA > 1 + epsilon) return false;
    if (tB < -epsilon || tB > 1 + epsilon) return false;

    return true;
}
```

### 关键步骤解释：
1. **线宽条件**：如果被覆盖线段的线宽（S.width）超过覆盖线段的线宽（T.width），则直接返回`false`。
2. **几何距离条件**：
   - 计算线段AB的直线方程。
   - 判断线段AB与CD是否平行。若平行，计算两直线的距离；否则距离为0（相交）。
   - 检查距离是否在允许范围内（`(T.width - S.width)/2`）。
3. **投影覆盖条件**：
   - 将线段AB的端点投影到线段CD的直线上，得到参数`t`。
   - 确保投影参数在`[0, 1]`区间内，确保线段AB的投影完全在CD的线段范围内。

该算法通过严格的数学条件判断，确保了线段覆盖的准确性。

#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>

// 定义一个二维点结构
struct Point {
    double x;
    double y;
};

// 计算向量差
Point operator-(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return { a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y };
}

// 向量加
Point operator+(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return { a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y };
}

// 向量和标量乘积
Point operator*(const Point &a, double s) {
    return { a.x * s, a.y * s };
}

// 计算点的欧氏范数
double norm(const Point &p) {
    return std::sqrt(p.x*p.x + p.y*p.y);
}

// 点乘
double dot(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y;
}

// 归一化向量
Point normalize(const Point &p) {
    double n = norm(p);
    return { p.x/n, p.y/n };
}

// 判断 p 是否落在由 A_start, A_end, 宽度 halfWidth 构成的胶囊区内
bool pointInCapsule(const Point &p, const Point &A_start, const Point &A_end, double halfWidth) {
    Point u = A_end - A_start;
    Point v = p - A_start;
    double uDotU = dot(u, u);
    double t = (uDotU > 0) ? dot(v, u) / uDotU : 0;
    t = std::max(0.0, std::min(1.0, t));
    Point proj = A_start + u * t;
    double d = norm(p - proj);
    return d <= halfWidth;
}

// 判断线段B是否完全被 A 覆盖
// A: from A_start to A_end with width wA, B: from B_start to B_end with width wB
bool isSegmentCovered(const Point &A_start, const Point &A_end, double wA,
                      const Point &B_start, const Point &B_end, double wB) {
    // 计算 B 的中心线方向及法向量
    Point vB = B_end - B_start;
    // 防止零长度
    if(norm(vB) < 1e-8) return false;
    Point dirB = normalize(vB);
    // 法向量取( -dirB.y, dirB.x )
    Point normalB = { -dirB.y, dirB.x };
    
    // 计算 B 区域的四个极值点（矩形顶点即可）
    double offset = wB / 2.0;
    Point P1 = B_start + normalB * offset;
    Point P2 = B_start - normalB * offset;
    Point P3 = B_end + normalB * offset;
    Point P4 = B_end - normalB * offset;
    
    // 检查每个点是否落在 A 定义的胶囊区中（A的半宽为 wA/2）
    double halfWA = wA / 2.0;

           pointInCapsule(P2, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P3, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P4, A_start, A_end, halfWA);
}

    Point A_end = {10, 0};

    Point B_start = {2, 0};

    ∑₍d=2₎^M (1/d) > ln M   （M ≥ 2 时成立）。
  令 M = ⌊√n⌋，则∑₍d=2₎^(⌊√n⌋) (1/d) > ln(√n) = (1/2) ln n.

2. ∑₍d=2₎^(⌊√n⌋) d  
  显然不超过所有从 2 到 √n 的数之和，即
    ∑₍d=2₎^(⌊√n⌋) d < ∑₍d=1₎^(√n) d = (√n(√n+1))/2 < n/2 + (√n)/2.

因此，当 n 足够大时，
  N₍合₎ ≥ n·(1/2 ln n) – (n/2 + (√n)/2)
       = n·[ (1/2 ln n – 1/2) ] – (√n)/2.
可以看出，当 n → ∞ 时，n·(1/2 ln n – 1/2) 主导增长，而 (√n)/2 可以忽略。也就是说，对于 n 足够大，
  N₍合₎ 的数量大致至少是 n·(1/2 ln n – 1/2)。

【与质数数目的比较】

另一方面，用一些初等方法可以证明（例如埃拉托斯特尼筛法的分析）质数数目 π(n) 的增长速度远低于 n，事实上有一种初等的不精确估计
  π(n) < n/(1 + ln 2)     （对于 n 较大时成立）。
更常见的估计是 π(n) ≈ n/ln n，但不使用 “质数定理” 也能证明，至少对于 n 足够大，有
  π(n) < n/2.
（例如，当 n ≥ 10 时，这一不严格的估计已成立。实际验证较小 n 可以另外处理。）

比较两边：
  合数个数 N₍合₎ ≳ n·(1/2 ln n – 1/2)
  质数个数 π(n) < n/2.
显然，当 n 足够大时，(1/2 ln n – 1/2) > 1/2，即合数的下界超过 n/2，从而有
  N₍合₎ > n/2 > π(n).

【结论】

于是我们证明了：对于 n 足够大，有 n 内的合数数目 n – π(n) 大于质数数目 π(n)（即合数比质数多）。

【总结说明】

1. 我们利用了每个合数都有一个不超过 √n 的最小质因子这个事实，从而对合数作了分类统计，得到了下界 n·(1/2 ln n – 1/2)。
2. 利用一项简单的不精确估计——对于 n 足够大，质数数目 π(n) < n/2——我们就看出合数个数最终会超过质数数目。
3. 这一证明只用了调和级数的简单下界、初等求和估计以及合数因子的基本性质，没有调用质数定理或其他高级结果。

这样，我们就给出了一个相对简单的证明：当 n 足够大时，n 内合数的数目确实多于质数。

**My Answer:**

Để đưa ra lời khuyên và kế hoạch phù hợp, chúng ta cần thực hiện các bước sau:

**1. Tính toán Năng lượng Tiêu thụ Hàng ngày (TDEE):**

*   **Tính BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate - Tỷ lệ trao đổi chất cơ bản):** Sử dụng công thức Mifflin-St Jeor cho nam giới:
    BMR = (10 × cân nặng [kg]) + (6.25 × chiều cao [cm]) – (5 × tuổi [năm]) + 5
    BMR = (10 × 110) + (6.25 × 168) – (5 × 34) + 5
    BMR = 1100 + 1050 – 170 + 5 = 1985 kcal/ngày
*   **Tính TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure - Tổng năng lượng tiêu thụ hàng ngày):** Vì bạn làm văn phòng và chưa tập gym, mức độ hoạt động của bạn được xem là "ít vận động". Chúng ta nhân BMR với hệ số hoạt động 1.2:
    TDEE = BMR × 1.2 = 1985 × 1.2 ≈ 2382 kcal/ngày
    Đây là lượng calo cơ thể bạn cần để duy trì cân nặng hiện tại với lối sống hiện tại.

**2. Đánh giá Mục tiêu Giảm cân:**

*   **Mục tiêu:** Giảm 20 kg trong 3 tháng (khoảng 90 ngày).
*   **Lượng calo cần thâm hụt:** Để giảm 1kg mỡ, cần thâm hụt khoảng 7700 kcal. Vậy để giảm 20kg, cần thâm hụt tổng cộng 20 × 7700 = 154,000 kcal.
*   **Thâm hụt hàng ngày:** 154,000 kcal / 90 ngày ≈ 1711 kcal/ngày.
*   **Lượng calo nạp vào mục tiêu:** TDEE - Thâm hụt hàng ngày = 2382 - 1711 = 671 kcal/ngày.

**Cảnh báo Quan trọng:** Mức calo nạp vào 671 kcal/ngày là **quá thấp, không an toàn và không bền vững**. Việc thâm hụt calo quá lớn (1711 kcal/ngày) có thể gây ra nhiều vấn đề sức khỏe nghiêm trọng như mất cơ, mệt mỏi cực độ, thiếu hụt dinh dưỡng, rối loạn trao đổi chất, và khó duy trì lâu dài. Mục tiêu giảm 20kg trong 3 tháng là rất tham vọng và tiềm ẩn rủi ro.

**Khuyến nghị:** Nên đặt mục tiêu giảm cân thực tế và an toàn hơn, ví dụ:
*   Giảm 0.5 - 1 kg/tuần (tương đương thâm hụt 500 - 1000 kcal/ngày).
*   Với mức thâm hụt 800-900 kcal/ngày (ví dụ, nạp vào ~1500 kcal/ngày), bạn có thể giảm khoảng 0.8-1 kg/tuần, tức là khoảng 10-12 kg trong 3 tháng. Đây là mục tiêu khả thi và an toàn hơn nhiều.
*   Để đạt mục tiêu giảm cân nhiều hơn, **bắt buộc** phải kết hợp việc tăng cường vận động (tập thể dục) để tăng TDEE và tạo thêm thâm hụt calo một cách lành mạnh.

**3. Phân chia Macros (Cho mức 1500 kcal/ngày - Ví dụ):**

Dựa trên mức calo mục tiêu an toàn hơn là 1500 kcal/ngày, một tỷ lệ phân chia dinh dưỡng đa lượng (macros) hợp lý có thể là:

*   **Protein (Chất đạm): 40%** (Giúp no lâu, duy trì cơ bắp)
    *   (1500 kcal × 0.40) / 4 kcal/g ≈ 150g Protein
*   **Carbohydrate (Tinh bột): 30%** (Cung cấp năng lượng, ưu tiên carb phức tạp)
    *   (1500 kcal × 0.30) / 4 kcal/g ≈ 113g Carb
*   **Fat (Chất béo): 30%** (Cần thiết cho hormone và sức khỏe, ưu tiên chất béo không bão hòa)
    *   (1500 kcal × 0.30) / 9 kcal/g ≈ 50g Fat

**4. Meal Plan Mẫu (Tham khảo ~1500 kcal):**

Đây chỉ là ví dụ, bạn cần điều chỉnh theo sở thích và thực phẩm sẵn có. Quan trọng là chọn thực phẩm nguyên chất, ít chế biến.

*   **Bữa sáng (~350 kcal):**
    *   50g yến mạch nấu với nước + 1 muỗng whey protein (~270 kcal, 30g P, 30g C, 4g F)
    *   Thêm 50g quả mọng (berries) (~25 kcal, <1g P, 6g C, <1g F)
    *   *Hoặc:* 3 lòng trắng trứng + 1 trứng nguyên quả chiên ít dầu + 1 lát bánh mì đen (~300 kcal, 25g P, 15g C, 15g F)
*   **Bữa trưa (~450 kcal):**
    *   150g ức gà nướng/áp chảo (~250 kcal, 50g P, 0g C, 5g F)
    *   100g gạo lứt đã nấu (~110 kcal, 2g P, 23g C, 1g F)
    *   Rau củ luộc/hấp (bông cải xanh, cải bó xôi,...) ăn thoải mái (~50 kcal)
    *   1 muỗng cà phê dầu ô liu (~40 kcal, 0g P, 0g C, 5g F)
*   **Bữa phụ (~200 kcal):**
    *   1 hũ sữa chua Hy Lạp không đường (~100 kcal, 18g P, 7g C, 0g F)
    *   1 quả táo nhỏ (~80 kcal, <1g P, 20g C, <1g F)
*   **Bữa tối (~450 kcal):**

    *   150g khoai lang luộc/nướng (~130 kcal, 2g P, 30g C, <1g F)
    *   Salad rau xanh các loại với dấm (~30 kcal)
*   **Tổng cộng (ước tính):** ~1480 kcal, ~130g P, ~116g C, ~45g F (Các con số này có thể dao động).

**5. Lời khuyên Quan trọng Khác:**

*   **Tập luyện:** Vì bạn chưa từng tập gym, hãy bắt đầu từ từ.
    *   **Cardio:** Đi bộ nhanh 30-45 phút, 3-5 ngày/tuần. Tăng dần cường độ hoặc thời gian.
    *   **Tập kháng lực (Tạ):** Bắt đầu với 2-3 buổi/tuần tập các nhóm cơ chính với tạ nhẹ hoặc trọng lượng cơ thể. Việc này cực kỳ quan trọng để giữ cơ bắp khi giảm cân. Hãy cân nhắc thuê huấn luyện viên giai đoạn đầu để đảm bảo kỹ thuật đúng.
*   **Uống đủ nước:** Mục tiêu 2.5 - 3.5 lít nước mỗi ngày (tùy thuộc mức độ vận động và môi trường).
*   **Ngủ đủ giấc:** 7-8 tiếng/đêm giúp điều hòa hormone kiểm soát cơn đói và phục hồi cơ thể.
*   **Kiên nhẫn và nhất quán:** Giảm cân là một quá trình dài hạn. Đừng nản lòng nếu có những ngày không như ý.
*   **Theo dõi tiến độ:** Ghi lại cân nặng, số đo, hoặc chụp ảnh để thấy sự thay đổi.
*   **Tham khảo chuyên gia:** Với cân nặng hiện tại và mục tiêu giảm cân đáng kể, việc tham khảo ý kiến bác sĩ hoặc chuyên gia dinh dưỡng là rất nên làm để đảm bảo an toàn và hiệu quả.

**Tóm lại:** Mục tiêu giảm 20kg trong 3 tháng là không thực tế và không an toàn nếu chỉ dựa vào ăn kiêng. Hãy điều chỉnh mục tiêu, đặt mức calo hợp lý (~1500 kcal hoặc cao hơn tùy mức độ tập luyện), tập trung vào dinh dưỡng cân bằng, kết hợp tập luyện đều đặn và kiên trì.

Here's a step-by-step calculation of the Net Present Value (NPV):

1.  **Interpret Input Data:**
    *   The phrase "net revenue from the workshop each year is as follows: Year 1: 1,100..." strongly suggests the listed figures are annual net revenues.
    *   Fixed Asset Investment = 500 million VND
    *   Working Capital (WC) = 15% of Net Revenue for the year.
    *   Variable Costs = 70% of Net Revenue
    *   Fixed Costs (excl. depreciation) = 100 million VND/year
    *   Depreciation: 500 million / 4 years = 125 million VND/year (Straight-line, zero salvage)
    *   Tax Rate = 20%
    *   Cost of Capital = 12%

2.  **Calculate Initial Investment (Year 0):**
    *   Fixed Assets = 500
    *   Initial WC (required for Year 1) = 15% of Year 1 Revenue = 0.15 * 1,100 = 165
    *   Total Initial Investment (Outflow) = 500 + 165 = 665 million VND

3.  **Calculate Annual Operating Cash Flows (OCF):**
    *   Use the formula: OCF = (EBIT) * (1 - Tax Rate) + Depreciation
    *   EBIT = Revenue - Variable Costs - Fixed Costs - Depreciation

    *   **Year 1:**
        *   Revenue = 1,100
        *   EBIT₁ = 1,100 - (0.70 * 1,100) - 100 - 125 = 1,100 - 770 - 100 - 125 = 105
        *   OCF₁ = 105 * (1 - 0.20) + 125 = 84 + 125 = 209
    *   **Year 2:**
        *   Revenue = 1,150
        *   EBIT₂ = 1,150 - (0.70 * 1,150) - 100 - 125 = 1,150 - 805 - 100 - 125 = 120
        *   OCF₂ = 120 * (1 - 0.20) + 125 = 96 + 125 = 221
    *   **Year 3:**
        *   Revenue = 1,200
        *   EBIT₃ = 1,200 - (0.70 * 1,200) - 100 - 125 = 1,200 - 840 - 100 - 125 = 135
        *   OCF₃ = 135 * (1 - 0.20) + 125 = 108 + 125 = 233
    *   **Year 4:**
        *   Revenue = 1,100

        *   OCF₄ = 105 * (1 - 0.20) + 125 = 84 + 125 = 209

4.  **Calculate Changes in Working Capital (ΔWC):**
    *   Assume WC required at the end of year `t` is based on year `t`'s revenue.
    *   WC (end Year 0) = 165 (calculated above)

    *   ΔWC (during Year 2) = WC₂ - WC₁ = 172.5 - 165 = 7.5. Cash Flow = -7.5 (Outflow)
    *   ΔWC (during Year 3) = WC₃ - WC₂ = 180 - 172.5 = 7.5. Cash Flow = -7.5 (Outflow)

    *   *Note:* An alternative, common timing convention (used by Assistant B) assumes the change in WC needed for the *next* year occurs at the *end* of the current year. This shifts the WC cash flows one year earlier. Let's use B's convention for comparability.
        *   ΔWC Investment at end Year 1 (for Year 2): 172.5 - 165 = +7.5 (Outflow)

        *   ΔWC Investment at end Year 3 (for Year 4): 165 - 180 = -15 (Inflow)

- The working capital is expected to be gradually recovered and fully recovered at the end of project.

Determine the net present value (NPV) of the project, knowing that the project’s cost of capital is 12% per year

Below is one worked‐example showing one way to “solve” this type of problem. In our case the firm is planning on spending 500 million VND for fixed assets, and it must “tie up” working capital each year. (In our solution we assume that the working capital requirements are “built‐up” gradually so that the change from one year to the next is what matters, with the full working capital then “released” at the end of the project.) We also use the fact that – by assumption – net revenue “drives” several items (variable costs and the working‐capital requirement). One common interpretation of the wording is to “back out” the revenue numbers from the working capital statement. (That is, if working capital equals 15% of revenue, and if you are told that in Year 1 working capital is 1,100 million VND then revenue must have been about 1,100/0.15.) One acceptable answer is as follows.

──────────────────────────────
Step 1. Determine “Gross” (net) revenue in each year

We are told that the working capital requirement in each year equals 15% of net revenue. Thus, if we denote annual net revenue by R then
  WC = 0.15 × R  ⇒  R = WC/0.15.
For each year we obtain:
 Year 1: R₁ = 1,100/0.15 ≈ 7,333 million VND
 Year 2: R₂ = 1,150/0.15 ≈ 7,667 million VND
 Year 3: R₃ = 1,200/0.15 = 8,000 million VND
 Year 4: R₄ = 1,100/0.15 ≈ 7,333 million VND

──────────────────────────────
Step 2. Compute Operating Costs and Depreciation

• Variable costs are 70% of net revenue.
• Fixed costs (other than depreciation) are 100 million VND/year.

Also, the fixed assets cost 500 million VND and are depreciated straight‐line over 4 years (salvage is negligible). Therefore, annual depreciation = 500/4 = 125 million VND per year.

Let’s list the computations year‐by‐year.

For Year i use:
 Revenue = Rᵢ
 Variable Costs = 0.70 Rᵢ
 Fixed Operating Costs = 100
 Depreciation = 125

Thus EBIT (Earnings Before Interest and Taxes) is:
 EBIT = Rᵢ – (0.70 Rᵢ) – 100 – 125
    = 0.30 Rᵢ – 225

Now calculate for each year:

• Year 1: 
 R₁ ≈ 7,333 
 Variable costs ≈ 0.70×7,333 ≈ 5,133 
 ⇒ EBIT₁ = 0.30×7,333 – 225 ≈ 2,200 – 225 = 1,975 million VND

• Year 2:
 R₂ ≈ 7,667 
 Variable costs ≈ 0.70×7,667 ≈ 5,367 
 ⇒ EBIT₂ = 0.30×7,667 – 225 ≈ 2,300 – 225 = 2,075 million VND

• Year 3:

 ⇒ EBIT₃ = 0.30×8,000 – 225 = 2,400 – 225 = 2,175 million VND

• Year 4:
 R₄ ≈ 7,333 
 Variable costs ≈ 5,133 
 ⇒ EBIT₄ = 0.30×7,333 – 225 ≈ 2,200 – 225 = 1,975 million VND

The income‐tax rate is 20%, so:
 Tax = 0.20 × EBIT

Thus:

 Year 2 Tax = 0.20×2,075 = 415  
 Year 3 Tax = 0.20×2,175 = 435  
 Year 4 Tax = 0.20×1,975 = 395  

After‐tax operating income = EBIT – Tax.
Then, because depreciation is a non‐cash charge we add it back to get the operating cash flow (OCF).

So:
 OCF = (EBIT – Tax) + Depreciation

Compute each year:
• Year 1: OCF₁ = (1,975 – 395) + 125 = 1,580 + 125 = 1,705 million VND  
• Year 2: OCF₂ = (2,075 – 415) + 125 = 1,660 + 125 = 1,785 million VND  
• Year 3: OCF₃ = (2,175 – 435) + 125 = 1,740 + 125 = 1,865 million VND  
• Year 4: OCF₄ = (1,975 – 395) + 125 = 1,580 + 125 = 1,705 million VND  

──────────────────────────────
Step 3. Determine Working Capital Investments

Because the working capital is 15% of revenue, the “required” working capital at the end of each year is given. However, cash flows come from the changes in working capital. Define WC₀ = 0 at project start and then:
 WC₁ = 1,100  
 WC₂ = 1,150  
 WC₃ = 1,200  
 WC₄ = 1,100

So the incremental (year‐to‐year) changes are:
 Year 1: ΔWC₁ = 1,100 – 0 = 1,100   (investment, so cash outflow)
 Year 2: ΔWC₂ = 1,150 – 1,100 = 50   (additional investment)
 Year 3: ΔWC₃ = 1,200 – 1,150 = 50   (additional investment)
 Year 4: ΔWC₄ = 1,100 – 1,200 = –100  (a partial release during Year 4)

Also, “fully recovered at the end” means that at the project’s termination the remaining working capital of 1,100 million VND is retrieved (cash inflow).

──────────────────────────────

 • (We assume no WC cash flow at t = 0; the first WC investment is made at the end of Year 1.)

 • Additional WC investment: –1,100

Year 2 (t = 2):

 • At the end of the project the entire remaining WC (1,100) is recovered.
 Net CF₄ = 1,705 + 100 + 1,100 = 2,905 million VND

──────────────────────────────

Our discount factors are:
 Year 0: 1
 Year 1: 1/(1.12) ≈ 0.8929
 Year 2: 1/(1.12²) ≈ 0.7972  (1/1.2544)
 Year 3: 1/(1.12³) ≈ 0.7118  (1/1.4049)

       + (1,735 × 0.7972)
       + (1,815 × 0.7118)
       + (2,905 × 0.6355)

• Year 3 PV = 1,815 × 0.7118 ≈ 1,292.3

        = –500 + 1,924.3 + 3,139.0  
        = 4,563.3 million VND (approximately)

──────────────────────────────
Step 6. Conclusion

The net present value (NPV) of the project is about 4,563 million VND. (Some rounding is involved.)

1. The “reverse‐engineering” of revenue from the working capital requirement relies on the statement that WC is 15% of net revenue.
2. The working capital cash flows are taken as the changes year‐to‐year plus a full recovery at the end.

The NPV of the project is approximately 4,560–4,570 million VND (roughly 4.56 billion VND).

### Approach
The key insight is to recognize that the optimal sequence of gifts alternates between the smallest possible values (1 and 2) to maximize the number of gifts. This alternating sequence minimizes the number of candies used per gift while ensuring no two consecutive gifts are the same. 

The approach involves:
1. **Identifying the maximum possible number of gifts** by considering both even and odd-length sequences:
   - For an even number of gifts \( k \), the total candies used will be \( 3 \times (k/2) \).
   - For an odd number of gifts \( k \), the total candies used will be \( (3k - 1)/2 \).

2. **Calculating the maximum possible \( k \)** for both even and odd cases using integer division:
   - For even \( k \): \( k_{\text{even}} = 2 \times \left\lfloor \frac{n}{3} \right\rfloor \).
   - For odd \( k \): \( k_{\text{odd}} = 2 \times \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{3} \right\rfloor + 1 \).

3. **Returning the maximum value** between the two calculated values of \( k \).

### Solution Code
```python
def happyPresents(n):
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    k_even = 2 * (n // 3)
    k_odd = 2 * ((n - 1) // 3) + 1
    return max(k_even, k_odd)
```

### Explanation
- **Even Case Calculation**: For an even number of gifts \( k \), each pair of gifts (1, 2) uses 3 candies. The maximum \( k \) is derived by dividing \( n \) by 3 and scaling by 2.
- **Odd Case Calculation**: For an odd number of gifts \( k \), the sequence ends with an additional 1, leading to a slightly different formula. Here, we adjust \( n \) by 1 to fit the even case formula and then adjust back.

**My Answer:**

The concept of "distance" between two curves can mean different things depending on whether you care about the specific way the curves are traced (the parametrization) or just the geometric shape they represent.

Here are common approaches:

1.  **Parametrization-Dependent Distances (e.g., Lp norms):**
    *   **Idea:** Compare the position vectors of the two curves at corresponding parameter values. This requires the curves, say `γ₁(t)` and `γ₂(t)`, to be defined over the same parameter interval (e.g., `t` in `[0, 1]`). If they are not, you might need to rescale their domains first.
    *   **Common Metrics:**
        *   **L² Distance:** `d₂(γ₁, γ₂) = sqrt( ∫ ||γ₁(t) - γ₂(t)||² dt )`
        *   **L∞ (Supremum) Distance:** `d∞(γ₁, γ₂) = sup_t ||γ₁(t) - γ₂(t)||`
    *   **When to Use:** Useful if the parameter `t` has a specific meaning (like time) and you want to measure how far apart the points are at the *same time*.
    *   **Limitation:** Highly sensitive to how the curves are parametrized. Two parametrizations tracing the exact same geometric shape but at different speeds will have a non-zero distance using these metrics.
    *   **Estimation:** For continuous curves, numerical integration is needed. For curves represented by sampled points `γ₁[i]` and `γ₂[i]`, you can compute discrete sums/maxima: `sqrt( Σ ||γ₁[i] - γ₂[i]||² )` or `max_i ||γ₁[i] - γ₂[i]||`.

2.  **Parametrization-Invariant Distances (Geometric Distances):**
    *   **Idea:** Measure the similarity of the geometric shapes traced by the curves, regardless of the speed or starting point of the parametrizations.
    *   **Common Metrics:**
        *   **Hausdorff Distance:**
            *   Treats the curves `C₁` and `C₂` as sets of points.
            *   `d_H(C₁, C₂) = max { sup_{x∈C₁} inf_{y∈C₂} ||x - y||, sup_{y∈C₂} inf_{x∈C₁} ||x - y|| }`
            *   In words: Find the point on `C₁` that is farthest from *any* point on `C₂`, and vice versa. The Hausdorff distance is the larger of these two maximum distances.
            *   **When to Use:** Good for comparing shapes as point sets. Sensitive to outliers.
            *   **Estimation:** Typically computed using sampled points on both curves. For each point on curve 1, find its minimum distance to curve 2 (approximated by the samples on curve 2), take the maximum of these minimum distances. Repeat with roles reversed and take the overall maximum.
        *   **Fréchet Distance:**
            *   Considers the continuous mapping and order of points along the curves. Often explained with the "man and dog on leashes" analogy: it's the minimum leash length needed for a man on curve 1 and a dog on curve 2 to traverse their respective curves from start to end, without backtracking (though they can vary their speeds).
            *   `d_F(γ₁, γ₂) = inf_{α, β} sup_{t∈[0,1]} ||γ₁(α(t)) - γ₂(β(t))||`, where α and β are continuous non-decreasing reparametrizations.
            *   **When to Use:** Often considered a more natural distance for curves than Hausdorff, as it respects the connectivity and ordering.
            *   **Estimation:** Computationally more complex. Algorithms exist, especially for polygonal curves (sampled points connected by lines), often based on dynamic programming or analyzing a "free space diagram".

    *   **Reparametrize by Arc Length:** You can reparametrize both curves by their arc length, `s`. This standardizes the "speed" to be unit speed. This makes the Lp distance less sensitive to the original parametrization speed but still requires alignment of starting points.

Finds an optimal non-linear alignment between the points of two sequences to minimize a cumulative distance measure. There are several ways to “measure” the distance between curves, and the right method depends on exactly what you mean by distance. For example, you might want a distance that is

• Point‐wise (comparing points corresponding to the same parameter value),  
• Geometric (comparing the shape or image of the curves regardless of parameterizations), or  
• Invariant under reparameterizations (so that two curves representing the same “shape” have zero distance).

Below are a few common approaches:

──────────────────────────────
1. Hausdorff Distance

Definition: If you have two curves, say Γ₁ and Γ₂, viewed as sets in ℝⁿ, the Hausdorff distance is defined as

  d_H(Γ₁, Γ₂) = max{ supₓ∈Γ₁ inf_y∈Γ₂ ||x – y||, sup_y∈Γ₂ infₓ∈Γ₁ ||x – y|| } .

What it does: This distance considers each point on one curve and finds the shortest distance to the other curve, then takes the worst‐case (maximum) of these distances. It is well suited for comparing the geometric sets (or “shapes”) regardless of the particular parametrizations.

Estimation: In practice, you sample points along each curve, compute for each point its distance to the other set, and then take the maximum minimal distance.

──────────────────────────────
2. Fréchet Distance

Definition: The Fréchet distance is designed especially for curves and takes into account the continuity and the ordering of the points. It is often illustrated with the “dog and owner” analogy: If the owner walks along one curve and the dog along the other, both without backtracking, the Fréchet distance is the length of the shortest leash required so that they can walk along their respective curves from start to finish.

Mathematically it is given by

  d_F(γ, δ) = inf_{α,β} sup_{t∈[0,1]} ||γ(α(t)) – δ(β(t))|| ,

where α and β range over all continuous, increasing reparameterizations of [0, 1] that cover the domain of γ and δ respectively.

Use: It is particularly useful when the “flow” or traversal along the curve matters.

Estimation: There are algorithms available (especially in 2D) for approximating the Fréchet distance from sampled points.

──────────────────────────────
3. Pointwise Norms (When Parametrizations are “Synchronized”)

If you happen to have two parametrizations that are defined on (or reparameterized to) the same interval and are expected to “match up” (for example, if the curves have been reparameterized by arc length), you might measure

  d_∞(γ, δ) = supₜ ||γ(t) – δ(t)||

or an L₂‐type distance

  d_2(γ, δ) = (∫₀¹ ||γ(t) – δ(t)||² dt)^(1/2).

When to use: These metrics are useful if you know that corresponding parameter values are meaningful. They are not invariant under arbitrary reparameterizations.

──────────────────────────────
4. Reparameterization to a Common Domain

If your curves have different “speeds” (i.e., the same geometric curve is traveled at different rates), then reparameterizing both curves by a common quantity (such as arc length) can lead to a more meaningful pointwise comparison. Once both curves are expressed as functions of arc length (which is intrinsic to the geometry of the curve), you can then apply a pointwise norm (L∞, L₂, etc.).

──────────────────────────────

• If you care about the geometric “shape” and want a reparameterization invariant metric, use the Hausdorff or Fréchet distances.

There are several ways to “measure” the distance between curves, and the right method depends on exactly what you mean by distance. For example, you might want a distance that is

• Point‐wise (comparing points corresponding to the same parameter value),  
• Geometric (comparing the shape or image of the curves regardless of parameterizations), or  
• Invariant under reparameterizations (so that two curves representing the same “shape” have zero distance).

Below are a few common approaches:

──────────────────────────────
1. Hausdorff Distance

Definition: If you have two curves, say Γ₁ and Γ₂, viewed as sets in ℝⁿ, the Hausdorff distance is defined as

  d_H(Γ₁, Γ₂) = max{ supₓ∈Γ₁ inf_y∈Γ₂ ||x – y||, sup_y∈Γ₂ infₓ∈Γ₁ ||x – y|| } .

What it does: This distance considers each point on one curve and finds the shortest distance to the other curve, then takes the worst‐case (maximum) of these distances. It is well suited for comparing the geometric sets (or “shapes”) regardless of the particular parametrizations.

Estimation: In practice, you sample points along each curve, compute for each point its distance to the other set, and then take the maximum minimal distance.

──────────────────────────────
2. Fréchet Distance

Definition: The Fréchet distance is designed especially for curves and takes into account the continuity and the ordering of the points. It is often illustrated with the “dog and owner” analogy: If the owner walks along one curve and the dog along the other, both without backtracking, the Fréchet distance is the length of the shortest leash required so that they can walk along their respective curves from start to finish.

Mathematically it is given by

  d_F(γ, δ) = inf_{α,β} sup_{t∈[0,1]} ||γ(α(t)) – δ(β(t))|| ,

where α and β range over all continuous, increasing reparameterizations of [0, 1] that cover the domain of γ and δ respectively.

Use: It is particularly useful when the “flow” or traversal along the curve matters.

Estimation: There are algorithms available (especially in 2D) for approximating the Fréchet distance from sampled points.

──────────────────────────────
3. Pointwise Norms (When Parametrizations are “Synchronized”)

If you happen to have two parametrizations that are defined on (or reparameterized to) the same interval and are expected to “match up” (for example, if the curves have been reparameterized by arc length), you might measure

  d_∞(γ, δ) = supₜ ||γ(t) – δ(t)||

or an L₂‐type distance

  d_2(γ, δ) = (∫₀¹ ||γ(t) – δ(t)||² dt)^(1/2).

When to use: These metrics are useful if you know that corresponding parameter values are meaningful. They are not invariant under arbitrary reparameterizations.

──────────────────────────────
4. Reparameterization to a Common Domain

If your curves have different “speeds” (i.e., the same geometric curve is traveled at different rates), then reparameterizing both curves by a common quantity (such as arc length) can lead to a more meaningful pointwise comparison. Once both curves are expressed as functions of arc length (which is intrinsic to the geometry of the curve), you can then apply a pointwise norm (L∞, L₂, etc.).

──────────────────────────────
Quick Summary

• If you care about the geometric “shape” and want a reparameterization invariant metric, use the Hausdorff or Fréchet distances.
• If your parametrizations have been synchronized (for instance, by arc length), then a simpler pointwise norm can be used.
• In a computational setting, you will likely sample points along the curves and estimate these distances numerically.

How to proceed in practice:
1. Decide what “distance” means for your application.
2. If reparameterization invariance is important, consider using the Hausdorff or Fréchet distances.
3. Sample points along the curves (if they are given by continuous functions) and use a numerical algorithm:
  – For Hausdorff, for each sample on one curve, compute the minimal distance to the other and vice versa.
  – For Fréchet, there are dynamic programming algorithms available, particularly in 2D.
4. If the curves are already “aligned” or need to be meaningfully compared pointwise, consider reparameterizing to arc length and use a sup or L₂ norm.

This should give you a good roadmap for estimating distances between curves defined by different parametrizations.

**(1) Proof that $\det(A) \neq 0$:**

We are given that $A = (a_{ij})$ is an $n \times n$ real matrix satisfying the condition of strict diagonal dominance: $|a_{ii}| > \sum_{j \neq i} |a_{ij}|$ for $i = 1, 2, \cdots, n$.

We can prove $\det(A) \neq 0$ using two common methods:

*   **Method 1: Using Gershgorin Circle Theorem:**
    The Gershgorin Circle Theorem states that every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of the matrix $A$ lies within at least one of the Gershgorin disks $D_i$ in the complex plane, defined as:
    $D_i = \{ z \in \mathbb{C} : |z - a_{ii}| \le R_i \}$, where the radius $R_i = \sum_{j \neq i} |a_{ij}|$.
    The given condition $|a_{ii}| > \sum_{j \neq i} |a_{ij}|$ translates to $|a_{ii}| > R_i$.
    Consider any disk $D_i$. For any point $z$ in this disk, the triangle inequality gives $|z| \ge |a_{ii}| - |z - a_{ii}|$. Since $|z - a_{ii}| \le R_i$, we have $|z| \ge |a_{ii}| - R_i$.
    Because $|a_{ii}| > R_i$, we know $|a_{ii}| - R_i > 0$. Thus, for any $z \in D_i$, $|z| > 0$. This means that the origin $0$ is not contained in any Gershgorin disk $D_i$.
    Since all eigenvalues $\lambda$ of $A$ must lie in the union of these disks $\bigcup_{i=1}^n D_i$, and none of these disks contain $0$, it follows that no eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ can be equal to $0$.
    The determinant of a matrix is the product of its eigenvalues: $\det(A) = \prod_{i=1}^n \lambda_i$. Since $\lambda_i \neq 0$ for all $i$, their product $\det(A)$ must also be non-zero.

*   **Method 2: By Contradiction (Levy–Desplanques Theorem):**
    Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that $\det(A) = 0$. This means $A$ is a singular matrix. Therefore, the homogeneous linear system $Ax = 0$ must have a non-trivial solution, i.e., there exists a non-zero vector $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n)^T \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $Ax = 0$.
    Let $k$ be an index such that $|x_k| = \max_{1 \le j \le n} |x_j|$. Since $x \neq 0$, we must have $|x_k| > 0$.
    Consider the $k$-th equation of the system $Ax = 0$: $\sum_{j=1}^n a_{kj} x_j = 0$.
    We can isolate the diagonal term: $a_{kk} x_k = - \sum_{j \neq k} a_{kj} x_j$.
    Taking absolute values on both sides: $|a_{kk} x_k| = |\sum_{j \neq k} a_{kj} x_j|$.
    Applying the triangle inequality to the right side: $|a_{kk}| |x_k| \le \sum_{j \neq k} |a_{kj} x_j| = \sum_{j \neq k} |a_{kj}| |x_j|$.
    Since $|x_k|$ is the maximum absolute value among the components of $x$, we have $|x_j| \le |x_k|$ for all $j \neq k$.
    Therefore, $\sum_{j \neq k} |a_{kj}| |x_j| \le \sum_{j \neq k} |a_{kj}| |x_k| = |x_k| \left( \sum_{j \neq k} |a_{kj}| \right)$.
    Combining the inequalities: $|a_{kk}| |x_k| \le |x_k| \left( \sum_{j \neq k} |a_{kj}| \right)$.
    Since $|x_k| > 0$, we can divide both sides by $|x_k|$ to get: $|a_{kk}| \le \sum_{j \neq k} |a_{kj}|$.
    This contradicts the given condition that $A$ is strictly diagonally dominant: $|a_{kk}| > \sum_{j \neq k} |a_{kj}|$.
    Thus, our initial assumption that $\det(A) = 0$ must be false. Hence, $\det(A) \neq 0$.

**(2) Eigenvalues of the Adjugate Matrix $A^*$:**

From part (1), we established that $A$ is invertible because $\det(A) \neq 0$.
The relationship between a matrix $A$, its inverse $A^{-1}$, and its adjugate matrix $A^*$ is given by:
$A A^* = A^* A = (\det A) I_n$, where $I_n$ is the $n \times n$ identity matrix.
Since $A$ is invertible, we can write $A^* = (\det A) A^{-1}$.

Let $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \dots, \lambda_n$ be the eigenvalues of $A$. Since $A$ is invertible, all eigenvalues $\lambda_i$ are non-zero ($\lambda_i \neq 0$ for all $i$).
If $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$ corresponding to eigenvector $v$ (i.e., $Av = \lambda v$), then $A^{-1}v = \frac{1}{\lambda} v$. This means $1/\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A^{-1}$ with the same eigenvector $v$.

Now consider the action of $A^*$ on the eigenvector $v$:
$A^* v = ((\det A) A^{-1}) v = (\det A) (A^{-1} v) = (\det A) \left( \frac{1}{\lambda} v \right) = \frac{\det A}{\lambda} v$.
This shows that if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, then $\frac{\det A}{\lambda}$ is an eigenvalue of $A^*$.
Therefore, the eigenvalues of the adjugate matrix $A^*$ are:
$\mu_1 = \frac{\det A}{\lambda_1}, \mu_2 = \frac{\det A}{\lambda_2}, \dots, \mu_n = \frac{\det A}{\lambda_n}$.
